records.definition: The encrypted authenticated remote Queue Fabric socket protocol introduced by v0.9-dev5; it is a wire identity, not a durable queue-record identity.
Pre-HELLO exact numeric source-address gate applied to an accepted socket. It is an admission fact and never substitutes for cryptographic identity.
Listener-wide union of current peer exact IPv4 addresses used for the pre-authentication rejection gate; rebuilt after peer re-registration.
Second source-IP check after HELLO resolves source manager, principal and key id to a trusted peer.
Long-term pre-shared secret used to authenticate HELLO/CHALLENGE and derive per-connection directional session material; minimum 256 bits in dev5.
Non-secret identifier selecting transport key material. It is metadata, not authority.
Protocol-labelled managers/channel/principal/key-id and client/server nonces bound into per-connection key derivation and secure-frame authentication.
Client-to-server direction with independently derived ChaCha20 key, HMAC key and nonce.
Server-to-client direction with independently derived ChaCha20 key, HMAC key and nonce.
queue.transport/2 wrapper carrying protocol identity, direction, ciphertext and HMAC tag.
Protect plaintext with ChaCha20, authenticate the resulting ciphertext/transcript/direction with HMAC-SHA-512, and verify the MAC before decrypting.
Current lifecycle in which a TCP session carries one DELIVER or PROBE and one RESULT or HEALTH response, allowing each derived directional nonce to be used once.
Durable receiver-side idempotence identity for legitimate retransmission. It is distinct from cryptographic session replay separation.
Property intentionally not claimed by the dev5 PSK design; a future standards-qualified ephemeral/TLS transport may add it.
Network-layer security rule permitting the Queue Fabric TCP port only from one exact peer IPv4. Queue Fabric itself stores the same address without CIDR notation.
Production boundary where trusted runtime code should resolve PSK material by reference; Queue Transport should not persist or become authority over long-term secrets.
Suggested durable node ability for allocator hard eligibility when remote dispatch depends on queue.transport/2.
Listener counter for connections rejected by the pre-authentication source-IP gate.

provenance.claim: Glossary derives from the secure transport contract.
Deployment/replay/secret terminology derives from the two-node OCI contract.
